facts.statement: Nesotrochis was a genus of extinct flightless birds found only on the islands of the Greater Antilles in the Caribbean.
facts.quote: Nesotrochis is a genus of extinct flightless birds that were endemic to the islands of the Greater Antilles in the Caribbean.

facts.statement: Although often called cave rails, Nesotrochis is now classified as an independent lineage of gruiform birds rather than a true rail.
facts.quote: They have often been called cave rails, though they are no longer considered true rails, but an independent lineage of gruiform birds.

facts.statement: Three species of Nesotrochis are known from subfossil remains discovered in cave deposits dating to the Late Pleistocene and Holocene.
facts.quote: It contains 3 species known from subfossil remains of Late Pleistocene and Holocene age found in cave deposits.

facts.statement: A 2021 DNA analysis of the mitochondrial genome of N. steganinos confirmed that the genus is not a rail but an independent lineage of gruiform birds.
facts.quote: In 2021, DNA analysis of a complete mitochondrial genome of N. steganinos indicated that they were not rails but an independent lineage of gruiform birds

facts.statement: Research suggests the closest relatives of Nesotrochis are the African family Sarothruridae and the extinct New Zealand adzebills.
facts.quote: with their closest relatives being the family Sarothruridae native to Africa, Madagascar, New Guinea and Wallacea, and the extinct adzebills of New Zealand.

facts.statement: Nesotrochis debooyi, the Antillean cave rail, was found in Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands.
facts.quote: Antillean cave rail, Nesotrochis debooyi (Puerto Rico, U.S. Virgin Islands)

facts.statement: Nesotrochis picapicensis, the Cuban cave rail, was found in Cuba.
Nesotrochis steganinos, the Haitian cave rail, was found on Hispaniola in Haiti.
facts.quote: Haitian cave rail, Nesotrochis steganinos (Hispaniola - Haiti)

facts.statement: Nesotrochis species are considered examples of insular gigantism and convergent evolution because their bodies were larger than those of actual rails.
facts.quote: Due to their similar but larger body dimensions when compared to actual rails, the West Indian cave rails are considered examples of insular gigantism, as well as of convergent evolution.

facts.statement: Nesotrochis fossils date from the Late Pleistocene to the Holocene.
The time range for Nesotrochis is from 0.129 million years ago to the present (0 million years ago).
facts.quote: Time range: Late Pleistocene to Holocene (0.129 to 0 million years ago)

facts.statement: The parent group for the genus Nesotrochis is the family Nesotrochidae.
The type species of the genus Nesotrochis is Nesotrochis debooyi.
